question: After fixing native-block suppression, should `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND` and `isToolProgressPayload` become a permanent public plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The native-block defect has a mechanical repair, but exposing generic cross-channel progress semantics to third-party plugins creates a lasting compatibility commitment that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve public contract
options.body: Keep the generic marker, document its transient-only semantics and expected channel behavior, and add focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Narrow to internal contract
options.body: Preserve typed Codex-to-Slack intent while removing the new third-party plugin SDK exports.

recommendation.title: Approve public contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic marker, document its transient-only semantics and expected channel behavior, and add focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history connects this person most strongly to the native Slack data path and shared reply-payload architecture affected by the decision.
